title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — When a Contractor-Missed Visit Earns a Credit
content:
## Training sheet: the missed visit credit

**When is a visit "missed"?** Where the contractor fails to perform a booked visit under the Preventive Maintenance Agreements and does not rebook it inside the tier's grace period, the customer is credited for the missed visit. The grace period is counted in business days from the day the visit was booked for, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and the office holidays published for the year, and a visit rebooked on the final grace day is still timely. A credit is issued only when the booked visit was not performed inside the tier's grace period counted from the day the visit was booked for. The booked day and the completion day are read from the visit entries on the agreement's history; the grace period is the tier's figure on the dispatch bulletin.

**Where does the boundary fall?** Take a hypothetical visit booked for a Monday at a tier with a 3-business-day grace period and no holiday in the week: business day 1 is Tuesday, day 2 Wednesday, day 3 Thursday. A visit performed on that Thursday is inside the grace period and earns no credit; a visit still unperformed after Thursday has been missed and earns one.

**What was the credit worth under the former basis?** The clause "The credit is the per-visit value of the agreement — the annual price divided by the tier's credited visits for the term — multiplied by the tier's missed visit credit rate, and at the top tier that rate exceeds the per-visit value because the agreement carries a performance guarantee." is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis. The tier figures it referred to remain published figures of the tier: the credited visits for the term used as the divisor are 4 at the Filter & Belt Service Plan, 2 at the Inspection Agreement, 8 at the Preventive Maintenance Agreement, 8 at the Labor Coverage Agreement, 10 at the Full Coverage Agreement and 18 at the Comprehensive Performance Agreement, and the missed visit credit rate and grace period are those on the dispatch bulletin.

**How is the credit applied?** The credit is applied to the next installment invoice rather than refunded.

**Which visits never earn a credit?** A visit the customer moved, and a visit closed as no-access, never produce a credit.

| Situation on the visit entries | Credit |
|---|---|
| booked visit not performed, and not rebooked, inside the grace period | yes |
| booked visit performed inside the grace period | no |
| booked visit rebooked on the final grace day | no |
| the customer moved the visit | no |
| the visit was closed as a no-access call | no |

superseded_clauses: The credit is the per-visit value of the agreement — the annual price divided by the tier's credited visits for the term — multiplied by the tier's missed visit credit rate, and at the top tier that rate exceeds the per-visit value because the agreement carries a performance guarantee.
